title: UNMASKING AND IMPROVING DATA CREDIBILITY: A STUDY WITH DATASETS FOR TRAINING HARMLESS LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Applying a k-NN label clusterability hypothesis and noise transition matrix estimation to score instances and mathematically detect subjective human annotation errors and inconsistencies across large-scale safety and toxicity datasets.

Qualitative evaluation of detected label errors demonstrating that human annotators subjectively misclassify text from opposing political standpoints as harmful (e.g., terms like "progressive-to-the-point-of-insanity") despite lacking explicitly toxic content.

Identifying and correcting false negative label errors in toxicity datasets where offensive stereotypes or prejudiced statements about Islam and Muslims were originally incorrectly marked as harmless by human annotators.

Detecting mislabeled safety preferences and label errors in RLHF conversational datasets for prompts that contain insults, derogatory stereotypes, or offensive language targeting specific nationalities (e.g., French people, Mexicans).
